name: Incident / Emergency
purpose: Represent an authority-declared operational or emergency incident with severity, revisioned impact, containment, restoration, resolution and review while keeping observations, problems, defects, tasks, communications and cyber qualification in their own masters.

owns: incident class and governing definition binding
incident-scoped actual or potential impact assessments
containment restoration resolution and closure assertions
delegates: underlying observations and occurrence identity to WM-MAT-008 and WM-ACT-015
persistent underlying problem identity to WM-KNW-014
response and remediation work to WM-ACT-006
public or addressed alerts to WM-ACT-027
excludes: automatic incident creation from an observation or alert
closure cascade to problems defects claims or tasks
merging operational and cyber incident identity

relations.purpose: Resolve occurrence evidence that supported declaration.
Resolve observations and measurements without copying their identity.
Resolve persistent problems and cause claims.
Resolve software defects implicated in the incident.
Resolve containment restoration and remediation tasks.
Correlate an independently governed cyber incident qualification.

invariants: An observation occurrence alarm or report never becomes an incident without an authorized declaration decision.
Every incident declaration pins the definition revision used.
Operational incident and cyber incident retain distinct identities even when supported by the same events.
Severity assessments name their scales and never overwrite earlier assessments.
Impact assessments distinguish actual from potential impact.
Impact assessments retain assessor method effective time affected scope and evidence.
Contained restored resolved and closed are distinct states and times.
Restoration never proves root cause elimination.
Incident closure never closes a problem defect task communication or cyber incident.
Problem and defect references are many-to-many and never become incident identity components.
Task priority remains task-owned and is not derived by copying incident severity.
Alerts and communications remain independently identifiable delivery records.
Resolution records retain outcome residual risk authority and evidence.
Reopening preserves prior resolution closure and review history.
Personal or sensitive impact evidence is disclosed only through governed projections.
